newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen in horizontal trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen in horizontal trend.

text.p: Polish shares rose in lower turnover on Friday but analysts said the market was likely to stay flat on Monday as investors were still waiting for impulses to spur an uptrend or a fall.

The main market's WIG index rose 93.0 points, or 0.7 percent, to 13,789.7, and turnover fell 7.9 percent to 77.4 million zlotys ($27.6 million) on both markets as 58 issues rose, 12 fell and 13 were flat.
"I don't expect a major price movement on Monday...there are no signals to spur growth or a fall," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

Some analysts said the bourse was likely to maintain its sideways drift throughout the week, but some chartists saw a possibility for growth after the consolidation period that has lasted for most of this month.
Continuous trade turnover was at 4.3 million zlotys ($1.5 million) with four stocks falling, two rising and one staying flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.3 percent in 14.1-million-zloty ($5 million) continuous trade and were flat in a 22.2-million-zloty ($7.9 million) turnover in the regular bourse session.
